newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan proposes China-Taiwan-HK joint-venture bank.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan proposes China-Taiwan-HK joint-venture bank.

text.p: Taiwan, China and Hong Kong business heavyweights are considering forming a joint-venture bank in Hong Kong to promote commercial links across the Taiwan Strait, a Taiwan business leader said on Wednesday.

"We have proposed the idea to our Hong Kong and mainland Chinese counterparts to jointly set up a bank in Hong Kong," an aide to Hsu Sheng-fa, chairman of Taiwan's Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry, quoted Hsu as saying.
"They are very interested in the proposal," the aide.
Hsu made the proposal in a meeting with visiting business delegations from Hong Kong and the communist mainland, Taiwan's diplomatic arch rival since a civil war split them in 1949.
"But it's only an idea. We haven't discussed it in detail," Hsu's aide told Reuters by telephone.
The mainland delegation was led by Jing Shuping, chairman of Beijing's semi-official All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce.

The Hong Kong and China entrepreneurs were in Taiwan for an unofficial economic forum, the first large-scale cross-strait contact since the Taiwan government's November announcement of freeze on cooperative initiatives with China.

The freeze was ordered as a reprisal following Beijing's successful courtship of South Africa, one of just 30 states that still recognise Taiwan's exiled Republic of China rather than the communist People's Republic on the mainland.
Taiwan has banned direct contact -- including banking communications -- with China since a civil war separated them in 1949. All contacts must be conducted through a third region, usually Hong Kong.

Despite the ban and a 17-month-old deadlock in unofficial Taiwan-China talks, some 30,000 Taiwan-funded businesses have poured more than US$20 billion into China since relations began to thaw in the late 1980s.
